slices.focus: After a spring island visit, Ayaka's grandparents become more candid about how delayed cargo affects household decisions, deepening her understanding of the stakes.
slices.summary: Ayaka visits Shikanoshima and hears her grandfather's blunt critique about mainland staff underestimating how people ration supplies when worried about the next boat. Calls with both grandparents become more frequent, more honest, and more detailed — grandmother Fumiko now gives field reports on medicine timing, grocery shelf thinness, and anxious neighbors. Ayaka struggles to separate operational insight from emotional weight.
